clue.text: Messy American students OTT? Time to be quiet

parts.note: L is a learner, so two learners make LL, students

indicators.note: time is to be quiet: the letter for time in the phrase gives way to a call for hush

SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: An American complains that excessive students are too noisy and demands silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The T that goes is the first letter of TOP, which becomes SHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the shop is an informal idiom for scattered and disorganised, so it describes something messy.

clue.text: British secret agent working on wiretaps to ensnare the Guardian

letters at work are being processed and rearranged, so these are reworked

the Guardian setter speaks for the paper, which is us

explanation.surface: A British spy operating on phone taps tries to catch out a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin Powers is the spoof spy of the Mike Myers films.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin Powers is the comic fictional British spy, a parody of James Bond, in a series of film comedies.

clue.text: Deliberately gave nothing to would-be borrowers

parts.note: giving money to would-be borrowers, as the clue goes on to say, is lending it
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: Someone pointedly refused to give anything to those asking for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical direction meaning slowly, so it describes playing deliberately.

clue.text: Leave boxing action, regularly missing jab

indicators.note: a box holds something inside, so one piece encloses the other

explanation.surface: A boxer quits the ring after a match, oddly without throwing a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing and jab both pretend to be from the ring; jab is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To jab someone informally means to give them an injection, which is how you vaccinate.

clue.text: Look up, eating half of cold dry cheese

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: taken as written, then cut to its first half
TT stands for teetotal, someone dry

explanation.surface: Someone checks the larder and finds a dry cheese half-eaten by the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft white Italian cheese made from whey.

clue.text: That man tells stories, including primarily clever twists

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man

indicators.note: including puts something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of clever is used

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A storyteller is praised for weaving clever plot twists.
explanation.definitionFit: Helices is the plural of helix, a spiral, so they are twists in a coiled shape.

clue.text: Muslim belonging to a student group rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: being in a group means belonging to it
the NUS is the UK's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A Muslim student is turned away from a campus society.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunni is a follower of the larger of Islam's two main branches.

clue.text: Everybody warned to ignore odds during sporting tie

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a one-all score is a draw in a match

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones of warned

parts.note: taken as written; its second, fourth and sixth letters are kept

explanation.surface: Everyone was told not to bet on the result of a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: One and all is an idiom meaning every single person, i.e. everybody together.

clue.text: Very pleasant detailed figure in computer game

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A finely detailed character in a video game is very pleasing to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic the Hedgehog is the blue mascot character of Sega's famous video game series.

clue.text: Enterprise spacecraft is a vessel with holes in it

parts.note: an enterprise is a business, a company
a lander is a craft that sets down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: The starship Enterprise is a ship whose hull is full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: Enterprise and vessel both call up Star Trek's starship; the vessel here is a kitchen bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl used to drain food, a kitchen vessel full of holes.

clue.text: Random few one's found in East London area that's swinging

indicators.note: random letters are in no set order, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed with the other letters
one's is one is, the letter I and IS's S
Wapping is a riverside district in East London

explanation.surface: A handful of people found in an East End district are into swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping is a district of East London by the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging in the slang sense is couples exchanging sexual partners, which is what wife-swapping describes.

clue.text: Person ridiculing authoritarian approach, but not loudly

indicators.note: but not means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: ruling with an iron fist is a harsh, authoritarian approach
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a tyrannical style of government, though quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironist uses irony, saying the opposite of what is meant, often to mock or deride.

clue.text: Conservative greeting opponent, a red

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
someone anti a thing opposes it

explanation.surface: A Tory says hello to a political enemy, a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: A red pretends to be a communist facing the Conservative; it is a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so it is one example of a red.

clue.text: Bread is mine — cheers!

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Someone claims the bread for themselves and offers thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow, slightly leavened bread from the Middle East and Mediterranean.

clue.text: Orchestra leader to look over popular overture from Ives

parts.note: taken as written
to scan is to look over quickly
in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the overture is the opening, so just the first letter of Ives

parts.note: Charles Ives, the American composer; his first letter

explanation.surface: A conductor studies a popular overture by the composer Charles Ives.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, the leader of an orchestra.

clue.text: Ally of Liberal abandoning party in iffy seat

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
iffy means dodgy or unsound, so the letters are in a bad order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the Liberal abandons the party, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a social is a party

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's ally quits the party to take a shaky seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An associate is a partner or companion, someone allied with you.

clue.text: Fickle character, clumsy actor and English stars in vacuous cartoon

indicators.note: these pieces sit inside the other
vacuous means empty, so the middle of cartoon is emptied out

parts.note: taken as written, then emptied to its outer letters
a ham is an overacting, unskilled actor
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A bumbling actor and an English star appear in an empty-headed animation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon changes its colour, so figuratively it is an inconstant person who keeps changing views.

clue.text: Drunk grasps article on Latin work by Eliot

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: wasted is slang for drunk

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A drunk clutches an essay on Latin poetry by Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Waste Land is T. S. Eliot's landmark 1922 modernist poem.

clue.text: What diner did with pork pie recipe in drawer here?

parts.note: a diner eats, so in the past ate
pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie
R is from Latin recipe, take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A diner tells of eating a pork pie from a recipe kept in a kitchen drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie. The drawer is not furniture but someone who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's workshop or studio, where someone who draws does their work.

clue.text: Couple on date in Parisian area showing some guts

parts.note: a duo is a couple, a pair
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A couple out on a date in a Paris district reveal plenty of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodena, plural of duodenum, are the first parts of the small intestine, so some guts.

clue.text: Precious metal base is shining

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
base means low, mean or ignoble

explanation.surface: A precious metal is said to make a dull base gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglow means glowing with light or warmth, so radiantly shining.

clue.text: Make concrete in Israel, building side of edifice

indicators.note: building puts the letters together in a new structure

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: a side is an edge, here the first letter of edifice

parts.note: its first letter, one edge of the word

explanation.surface: A builder in Israel pours concrete for one wall of a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: Concrete and building suggest construction, but make concrete means make real.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a plan or idea is to make it actual and real, i.e. to make it concrete.

clue.text: Hard to leave Confucian classic, which is topping

indicators.note: the letter for hard leaves, so it is taken out

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese Book of Changes, a Confucian classic

explanation.surface: A difficult passage is cut from the Book of Changes, which is still excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: Topping looks like British slang for excellent; it is a cake topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on top of a cake, so a topping.

clue.text: After engaging writers, publisher says what it thinks

indicators.note: engaging means taking on, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: Once it has hired some authors, a publishing house speaks its mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to speak frankly and reveal one's true feelings.

clue.text: Where tablets were given wrong kind of computer program

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
AI, artificial intelligence, is a type of software

explanation.surface: Tablets came loaded with the wrong sort of software.
explanation.walkthrough: Tablets look like computer tablets; they are the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is where, in the Bible, Moses received the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Shrink is probing antagonist of 1 down

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so one piece is put in the other

parts.note: Mini-Me is Dr Evil's diminutive clone, Austin Powers's foe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is analysing the villain of the Austin Powers films.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink looks like a psychiatrist, the probing one; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise is to reduce something to the smallest amount, to make it smaller.

clue.text: Day out in nude provoked dissatisfaction

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
the letter for day is out, removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A day out in the nude left someone feeling discontented.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weary dissatisfaction with life.

clue.text: What digital artist does with eg bit of whisky, say, and beer, drinking a mixed gin

parts.note: a finger is a measure of spirits, a finger's depth in a glass

parts.note: a pint is a beer
taken as written

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred around

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: An artist in the digital age gets through whisky, beer and a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Digital means using the digits, the fingers, rather than a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Finger-painting is painting with the fingers, which is literally what a digital artist does.
